target_customer: Rideshare and delivery drivers who pay a subscription
problem: Drivers juggle several apps on several phones and accept low value trips. Mystro runs Uber, Lyft and others together and auto accepts only trips that meet driver filters.
business_model: Driver subscription, reported at 11.95 dollars per month or 99.95 dollars per year in 2017

founders.name: Herb Coakley
founders.background_notes: Described as a former Uber driver who started Mystro, and as the person who began monetizing the app in 2017. He took about two years to find developer Matt Rajcok. Source is press coverage; he is not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Dwayne Shaw
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him with no background.

investors: A Google employee who was a passenger

technical_complexity.rationale: Reading and acting on trip offers inside Uber and Lyft apps without API access is fragile reverse engineering that breaks when the platforms update.

defensibility.rationale: The product depends on platform apps it does not control, and the idea can be copied. A driver community and filter settings give mild lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Uber sent letters accusing Mystro of violating its terms of service. Lyft later threatened to deactivate drivers using third party earnings apps. The app was still live with a 2025 update.

market_need_then: CNN and TechCrunch coverage in August 2017 described drivers running two phones and the app promising 30 to 33 percent more earnings. Demand shown by paying subscribers is stated by the company only.

branding.domain_note: Uses mystrodriver.com, a suffix domain on the product name
branding.brand_signature: Over 100,000 drivers claim and press mentions from CNN, WSJ, BBC and Forbes on the site

rebrands.why: App store title now covers delivery apps as well, no stated reason

branding.community_and_virality: The site links a Discord community and a podcast episode and reviews exist on The Rideshare Guy.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized among rideshare drivers through press and reviews, but sources give no brand specific measures.

outcome_analysis: Mystro raised only small money from a passenger angel and YC but reached a paying driver base and kept operating for years under pressure from Uber and Lyft terms of service enforcement. The YC directory lists it as inactive, but its own site and app store listing show it live with a claimed 100,000 drivers, so the inactive label looks stale. No shutdown was found.
notes: Exit is none because the app was active, which conflicts with the YC Inactive status. Competitors: no source dated near August 2017 was found for rival auto accept apps, so the list is empty; Gridwise and Para are analytics apps with undated pages. The 120K YC figure appears in CNN and in aggregators; investor lists in CB Insights and Village.ai conflict and are not recorded. The Google employee check is from CNN and press on Coakley, undated. Founders Shaw and Coakley are from different sources and no source ties them together.
